chapter: Discovering jazz and playing in Berlin
title: Buying Louis Armstrong records and Bill Haley
summary: Teenage enthusiasm; he distinguishes Louis records from big-band sound, mentions Bill Haley, and buys records as money allows.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And then they were still younger. And then they were still younger. They were still younger. Because it was a lot of young people. And then the flame was so over.
And you were suddenly very interested in the Jazz? Yeah, very interested. You noticed that was your music?

Yeah. But I noticed the difference between the albums I bought from Louis and the Big Band-Sachen, which I heard in concerts and in radio. And then was also Bill Haley very well. Was that not later? No, no.
Bill Haley and Scum. Yeah, that was the beginning. And so far my money was reached, I bought me then only the plates. And then I had to do this Louis-Serie. And then I had to do this.
